why: WHAT THE MASONRY OF THE TWO TARGETS ACTUALLY IS, AS NUMBERS.
The engine cuts a block into courses from three constants -- a rise, three
block lengths and a chamfer -- and those three were chosen before anybody
measured the targets. This file is the measurement. It is spec and not
mechanism: it says what the wall IS, and src/world/voxel/ says how a wall is
cut. The two are separate on purpose, because the second is the engine every
session builds on and the first is one session's reading of one picture.
EVERY NUMBER NAMES THE FILE IT WAS READ IN. Nothing here is a preference and
nothing here is rounded to look tidy: where the reading has a band, the band
is written down beside the value, and where two faces disagree both are kept.
A spec whose numbers cannot be traced back to a window of a target is a taste
with a schema on it.
AND IT IS NOT ALL CONSUMED YET. tools/monoliths/spec.mjs reports, line by
line, which of these the frozen engine door can express and which it cannot;
the ones it cannot are an escalation and not a silence.

camera: The fitted camera published in assets-src/materia/ricetta.json under
measuredBy.camera -- the V0c fit off the monolith silhouettes, NOT
POSE_VOX_DAY. That distinction carries weight after E-V8f: the two vox
poses were refitted to a walker of 1.80 m and moved by 66 to 74 px of
horizon, and nothing measured at them survives. This camera is a separate
fit against the target's own stone and did not move, so the readings below
measuredBy.residual: 2.4 px rms, 0.5 px median, over 96 silhouette points on the five blocks

why: A course is 0.215 m and the honest bar is the window spread, 0.203 to
0.227. The engine's COURSE 0.22 sits inside it, so this reading does not
contradict the constant -- and the argument about 0.21 against 0.22 is an
order of magnitude smaller than the thing that does matter, which is that
the courses of these walls are NOT ALL THE SAME HEIGHT and do not run
straight. A ruled grid is what these targets are not.
THE BLOCK OF THIS WALL IS ABOUT SQUARE, and that is the single largest
divergence between the targets and the engine's defaults. The engine cuts
0.22 / 0.44 / 0.66 on a 0.22 course, so its mean block is a course and a
half wide; the targets' mean block is one course wide. Doubles and triples
exist and are a minority, which is the tail past 0.30 m and not the body of
the distribution.
TWO MEANS ARE GIVEN AND NEITHER IS WRONG. inWindow is the mean over the
same window the course was pooled on, which is the number the aspect ratio
was formed from; overAll is the mean of the whole histogram including the
tail. Anything that counts blocks has to say which one it used, because the
two differ by a fifth and a count is linear in it.

histogram.why: counts by lower edge, pooled over 01-front, 04-front and 05-front

why: The joint of the recipe holds on stone without a change. It was fitted on
grass and the worry was that stone would want a darker or a wider one;
measured on five windows of stone with the campaign's own estimator
imported unchanged, it does not.
The arris is the same BRIGHTNESS as the recipe's and a different COLOUR.
The mandate expected stone to read a stronger chamfer than grass and it
does not: four windows give 1.072 to 1.091 against the recipe's 1.07-1.09.
What changes is the blue in it -- about twice the recipe's -- and that is a
material's number, so it belongs to whoever fits the stone and not to
whoever cuts it.
THE HEADS ARE STEPPED, NOT CRENELLATED. FASE 0 read them as a top course
with blocks missing; measured column by column they are two to four LEVELS
that drop over part of the width, which is a different shape and a
different generator. No upper face of any block is in frame -- the eye is
at 2.733 m and the lowest head is 4.84 -- so what FASE 0 read as tops were
the high courses seen from below.
THE LEVELS BELOW ARE RAW AND THE SUMMARY IS DERIVED FROM THEM, which is why
both are here. Two levels closer together than the merge distance are one
level, and that distance is DERIVED: a step of one course has to be told
apart from the WANDER of a course, which is 30 mm at the median and 35 at
p90, so three times the p90 -- 0.105 m, half a course -- is the separation,
by the same rule the campaign derives every other tolerance.
MERGING AT ONE WHOLE COURSE WAS TRIED FIRST AND IT WAS WRONG. It swallowed
01's 0.19 m drop, which is nearly a whole course read on 44% of the width,
and reported a head with one level on it. The rule that hides the finding
is worth writing down beside the one that does not.
SO: 1 to 4 levels at a tenth of the width, dropping 0.9 to 6.5 courses --
which CONFIRMS the coordinator's 1 to 6.5 courses and widens his 2-to-4
levels at the bottom end. 05 is the block that widens it: it carries one
level over half its width and a second notch at 9.7%, one tenth of a point
under the filter. Unmerged and unfiltered the same heads read 4 to 13
levels, which is the same wall counted without a rule.
metresUp is up the block from ITS OWN foot, so 03 is measured off the
platform it stands on and not off the meadow.
ERRATA. The six readings below are NOT the ones this file first carried,
and the correction is a change of WHERE THE BAND IS TAKEN and not of how
it is estimated. The line is still V2-AN's own (v2-pietra/an/muschio.mjs
section 5b: the median luminance of a band one course high under the top,
against the band two to four courses further down, with the campaign's
moss detector cutting the green out). What moved is the top.
The first reading put the band under the lid of the BOX layout.js
declares, because on a target a rectifier knows no other top. But the
stone the picture DRAWS stops lower than the box -- this same file states
both numbers in heads.perBlock, and on 04 they differ by 0.435 m -- so on
that block a third of the band was SKY, and sky over stone reads as a very
pale top course. That is the whole of the 2.370.
Taken under the drawn stone (targetHead, the same height heads.perBlock
median 1.103, and a band a fifth as wide. The finding survives -- the top
course IS paler than the stone three down, on all six faces -- and what
does not survive is the claim that one face is nearly two and a half times
its own body.
The band stays declared rather than averaged away, for the same reason it
always was: 01-left is 1.161 and 05-front is 1.008, and one law over one
wall cannot be both.

why: DECLARED BY FASE 0 AND NOT MEASURED, and it is written down rather than
carried as if it were a reading. The corner is a toothing of blocks and not
a straight line, which is what FASE 0 saw on the crops; V2-AN did not put a
number on it, because the two flanks that would show it best are 9 and 10
px wide. Whoever fits it measures it first.
WHERE THE STONE ACTUALLY STOPS, PER BLOCK, AGAINST THE BOX layout.js
DECLARES. The boxes are the input to the generator and they stay; what
changes is that the courses stop where the target's widest head level is,
not where the box's lid is. Read at the widest level on purpose, so a step
in the head is not mistaken for the head.
targetHead is metres up the block from its own foot. courses is that height
in whole courses of 0.215 m, which is the number a generator needs; the
residual of that rounding is stated because it is not free -- 05's box is
already right to a centimetre and quantising costs it 9.5 cm, which buys
04's 35 and 02's 13. The worst block goes from 0.35 m out to 0.10 m out.
The run layout.js declares is the run the target draws, and this is the one
line of the plan the measurement CONFIRMS rather than corrects: six steps,
a tread of 0.36 m, and a rise of 0.2167 m which is one course. Five nosings
were found at a spacing of 1.04 modelled steps.
AND THERE IS NO CYAN STRIP ON IT, by day or by night. The treads read blue
and green level with each other -- grey stone under a blue sky, the same
balance every shaded face in the picture carries -- while the marker beside
them reads B/G 1.14 and the engraved wall behind them 1.20. What does read
on a tread is the pale nosing, which is an arris and not a light.
The band the chapter declares, from the agreement of two independent
implementations -- and it was formed on 0.22 / 0.44 / 0.66 masonry. It is
kept here because a spec that halves the block width has to be counted
against it rather than beside it: tools/monoliths/spec.mjs does that
arithmetic and it does not come out inside the band.
